question.problem:
The point $P$ with coordinates $(2,-5)$ lies on the curve $y=f(7x).$ Find the point $Q$ that must lie on $y=f(x).$

The coordinates of $Q$ are $(${{field-1}}$,$
{{field-2}}$).$
question.worked_solution:
Since $f(x)=f(\frac{1}{7}\cdot (7x)),$ the function $y=f(x)$ represents a stretch of the function $y=f(7x)$ by a factor of $7$ parallel to the $x$-axis. This has the effect of multiplying the $x$-coordinates of all points on $y=f(7x)$ by $7.$

Therefore, the point $(2,-5)$ on $f(7x)$ is mapped to the point $(7\cdot 2,-5)=(14,-5),$ and this point must lie on the graph of $y=f(x).$
